title: Number Quest Unit 5 · The Hundreds Hedge (Launchpad)

items.q: Which number is 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones?
misconceptions: put the 7 in the tens place
wrote each part as its own number
items.why: 4 hundreds is 400. There are no tens, so write 0. Then 7 ones: 407.

misconceptions: read the middle digit as ones
mixed up the tens and hundreds places
items.why: The middle digit is in the tens place. So the 5 means 5 tens, or 50.

misconceptions: swapped the tens and the ones
read the parts from back to front
wrote each part in full, side by side
items.why: 600 is 6 hundreds, 30 is 3 tens and 8 is 8 ones. Together that is 638.

items.q: Count by tens: 230, 240, 250. What comes next?
items.why: Each step is 10 more. 250 and 10 more is 260.

misconceptions: looked at the tens and ones first
thought all three-digit numbers are the same size
picked a sign that does not compare
items.why: Look at the hundreds first. 3 hundreds is less than 4 hundreds, so 352 is less.

misconceptions: swapped the tens and the ones
looked only at the ones digit
items.why: The hundreds are the same, so look at the tens. 7 tens is more than 6 tens.

misconceptions: wrote the tens and the ones side by side
items.why: 8 ones and 7 ones make 15: one new ten and 5 ones. 3 tens, 2 tens and 1 ten make 6 tens.

misconceptions: took the smaller digit from the bigger each time
forgot the ten that was opened
items.why: Open a ten: 5 tens and 12 ones. Take away 2 tens and 5 ones. That leaves 37.

misconceptions: wrote the tens and the ones side by side
items.why: 6 ones and 4 ones make a new ten. 4 tens, 3 tens and 1 new ten make 8 tens: 80.
